overview: Haiti covers the western third of the island of Hispaniola, which it shares with the Dominican Republic. Its capital and largest city is Port-au-Prince. In 1804 Haiti became the first country founded by formerly enslaved people, after a successful revolution against French rule, and the second independent country in the Americas. Haitian Creole and French are its official languages.

geography.text: Haiti is very mountainous; its name comes from a Taíno word meaning 'land of high mountains'. Two long peninsulas reach west on either side of the Gulf of Gonâve. Earthquakes and hurricanes have caused great damage, including a devastating earthquake in 2010.

subsections.title: Climate
subsections.text: Tropical, with a hurricane season from June to November.

subsections.title: Wildlife
subsections.text: The Hispaniolan trogon, the national bird, lives in the mountain forests.

history.text: Haiti was the French colony of Saint-Domingue, the richest sugar colony in the world, worked by hundreds of thousands of enslaved Africans. In 1791 they rose up, and in 1804 Haiti became the first country founded by formerly enslaved people. Since then Haiti has faced dictatorship, foreign occupation, poverty and natural disasters.

events.title: French colony
events.text: Spain hands the western part of Hispaniola to France.

events.title: Revolution begins
events.text: Enslaved people rise up against the plantation system.

events.title: The 'independence debt'
events.text: France forces Haiti to pay huge compensation for its freedom.

events.title: Earthquake
events.text: A devastating earthquake strikes near Port-au-Prince.

government.text: Haiti is officially a semi-presidential republic, but its government has been in crisis since President Jovenel Moïse was assassinated in 2021. Elections have not been held for years, and armed gangs control much of the capital, Port-au-Prince. A transitional council and an international security mission have tried to restore order.

economy.text: Haiti is the poorest country in the Americas. Most people work in farming or informal jobs. Clothing is the main export, and money sent home by Haitians abroad makes up about a fifth of the economy. Earthquakes, hurricanes and violence have repeatedly set the country back.

culture.text: Haiti was the first country founded by formerly enslaved people, in 1804. Haitian Creole and French are its official languages. Its painters, vodou traditions and kompa music are famous, and soup joumou, a pumpkin soup eaten on Independence Day, is on UNESCO's heritage list.

items.title: Citadelle Laferrière
items.text: A huge mountain-top fortress built after independence.

items.title: Soup joumou
items.text: Pumpkin soup that celebrates freedom, listed by UNESCO.

items.title: Haitian art
items.text: Bright paintings sold in galleries and markets.

subsections.title: Food
subsections.text: Griot, fried pork with pikliz, a spicy pickled cabbage.

subsections.title: Music and arts
subsections.text: Haitian painting, metal sculpture and kompa music are famous.

subsections.title: Traditions and festivals
subsections.text: On Independence Day, 1 January, families eat soup joumou, listed by UNESCO.

sport.text: Football is Haiti's most popular sport. The men's team reached the World Cup in 1974, and the women's team played at its first World Cup in 2023. Haiti qualified for the 2026 men's World Cup.

items.text: Haiti scored against Italy's Dino Zoff, ending his record run without conceding.

didYouKnow: Haiti was the first country in the world founded after a successful revolt by enslaved people.
The Citadelle Laferrière is one of the largest fortresses in the Americas.

keyPeople.name: Toussaint Louverture
keyPeople.text: Led the uprising that ended slavery in Haiti.
